name: REPLACE-with-a-short-slug
objective: One sentence: what gets better, and for whom.
metric: Exact number and units, negated if smaller is better (higher is always better).

metric_set._comment: The request broken down. ONE fitness scalar (the `metric` above) plus everything the user would trade it against. Anything you would refuse to merge over belongs here and must be measured from the first candidate -- if it is only in your head, the search cannot see it.
metric_set.fitness: the scalar above; the only thing the loop maximizes

monitored.accuracy: REPLACE or delete: ULP / relative error, WORST case not mean. Mandatory if the candidate may reassociate, widen, narrow or approximate -- a search will find speed by spending precision
monitored.correctness_class: exact | bit-identical | within-tolerance -- say which, and what enforces it
monitored.footprint: REPLACE or delete: code size, .rodata, tables
monitored.memory: REPLACE or delete: allocation count, peak, stack depth
monitored.maintainability: REPLACE or delete: non-comment lines, function count, duplicated decision tables, number of code paths that must agree forever

metric_set.guards: metrics reported at weight 0.0 -- they catch regressions, they are not optimized
metric_set.thresholds: REPLACE: the bound on each monitored metric, and who owns the call when a candidate trades against it

contradiction: improving X worsens Y — the central trade strategists will work
invariants: results identical to baseline on all test inputs
correctness_gate: REPLACE: the command that proves a candidate still works, run inside the candidate dir
abstraction: solution | constructor | search-algorithm — and one line on why

evaluator._comment: Either a flat command (below), or `stages` for an evaluation cascade.

instruments._comment: What the harness can measure BESIDES the fitness scalar, and which question each one settles. A strategist with a mechanism hypothesis should be able to read this and test it for pennies instead of spending a candidate. Delete what does not apply; add what does. Everything listed here should be recorded per candidate in the evaluator's `metrics` dict so the population can be correlated later.
instruments.timing: the fitness metric, with spread and repeats
instruments.disassembly: REPLACE or delete: e.g. objdump of the hot region; instructions and branches per unit of work. Settles 'did the change land at all'
instruments.static_uarch: REPLACE or delete: e.g. llvm-mca on the hot loop. Settles latency-bound vs throughput-bound vs front-end-bound — usually the most valuable single fact, and expensive to infer from timing alone
instruments.counters: REPLACE or delete: e.g. perf stat branch-misses, cache-misses, IPC
instruments.allocations: REPLACE or delete: count and peak; mandatory for embedded/no_std/latency-sensitive targets
instruments.footprint: REPLACE or delete: e.g. size -A for .text/.rodata. Distinguishes a free win from one bought with tables
instruments.build_matrix: REPLACE or delete: other targets, opt levels, and the flags the product actually ships. A win at one flag combination is a fact about your build
instruments.noise_floor_cross_session: the seed re-scored in a LATER session; usually wider than the back-to-back floor and the one to trust

tuning_plan._comment: The triage of the change space, and how each half is searched. The LLM loop searches STRUCTURES; a script searches VALUES. Every axis of variation belongs to exactly one of them -- anything in neither list is the gap check 7 exists to catch. Reason about the response shape FIRST, then pick the method.

structural_only.what: REPLACE: the axis of variation that needs an LLM candidate
structural_only.why_not_a_value: REPLACE: one sentence. If you cannot write this sentence, it is probably parametric after all

automated_search._comment: Delete and set to null ONLY if nothing is parametric -- and then say why in structural_only. Runs BEFORE generation 1, and its winner is folded into the seed, so the loop starts from the best configuration of the current structure instead of rediscovering it.
automated_search.method: REPLACE: grid | random | coord | screening-then-narrow | bayesian | nsga-ii
automated_search.sizing: REPLACE with the arithmetic: axes x repeats x seconds-per-eval = wall clock. If the full grid fits, enumerate it -- exhaustive needs no assumptions and returns the whole surface. 'Too big' without this arithmetic means nobody did the arithmetic

parameters.name: REPLACE: e.g. BLOCK_THRESHOLD
parameters.expected_response: REPLACE: monotonic | unimodal | multi-modal | step/threshold | interacting-with-X -- and WHY you think so
parameters.sensitivity_checked: REPLACE: does sweeping the whole domain move the metric by more than the noise floor? If NO, the benchmark cannot tune this -- say so and argue the value from the input distribution instead of fitting noise
parameters.method: binary/ternary search | full sweep | exhaustive | factorial grid | Latin hypercube | coordinate descent | Morris screening | Bayesian (GP/TPE) | CMA-ES | NSGA-II | GA
parameters.validation: REPLACE: tuned on which set, confirmed on which held-out set

tuning_plan.resolution: the minimum detectable difference = the noise floor. You cannot tune finer than this; state it
tuning_plan.multi_objective: If objectives genuinely compete (speed vs size vs accuracy), return a Pareto front via NSGA-II rather than a scalarised single point, and let the owner pick
tuning_plan.meta_parameters: Do NOT tune the search's own knobs on the run you are reporting -- that fits the searcher to the instance. Use defaults and say so, or tune on a different problem

input_coverage._comment: Filled during gate check 5. What the benchmark's inputs look like next to production's, and what the metric cannot see.
input_coverage.distribution_source: REPLACE: where the real input distribution was measured, with n
input_coverage.shapes: REPLACE: each scored shape, its weight, and the SOURCE of that weight (measured call frequency, or an explicit product decision)
input_coverage.guards: REPLACE: shapes carried at weight 0.0 — reported, never scored. A shape that exists so something 'must not collapse' belongs here, not in the weighted metric
input_coverage.blind_spots: REPLACE: input families the metric does NOT contain, named explicitly so they stop being invisible

interpretation.success: gain > noise floor, holds on held-out and on the worst input shape
interpretation.non_result: gain inside the noise floor — report and stop, do not rerun hoping
interpretation.abandon_if: state the condition now, before anyone has seen a number

risks: from the pre-mortem: what would make this run worthless three days from now
notes: Where held-out inputs live, what a cheating solution would look like, anything the next reader needs.
